body:
> I'm not sure if it's a correct solution. Didn't see similar code in other gizmos and they don't have this problem.

Seems like clicking any `Path3DEditorPlugin`'s toolbar button results in redrawing every existing `Path3DGizmo` (redraw is connected to the `pressed` signals in the gizmo's constructor and not disconnected until the gizmo is freed):
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/18a63d15e944eaaa107b2f37ebf40893c751ce20/editor/scene/3d/path_3d_editor_plugin.cpp#L590-L594

I'm not familiar with the 3D gizmos logic, but probably clicking these buttons should update/redraw only the currently selected/active gizmos, instead of all existing `Path3DGizmo`s.
Or maybe non-active gizmos should be freed instead in the first place (and recreated only when needed)?

Nevertheless, the check/guard currently added in this PR makes sense on its own, regardless of the redundant/unneeded gizmo redraws.

> Nevertheless, the check/guard currently added in this PR makes sense on its own, regardless of the redundant/unneeded gizmo redraws.

I'm not convinced tbh. No other gizmo has such guards.

I think I found the problem. The button signals should be connected to path's `update_gizmos()` instead of `redraw()`. Also seems like once a Path3D gizmo is created, the buttons will update it forever, which is bad if you have lots of paths in your scene. The editor seems to be wrongly implemented.
